item.title: MiBeeSteward: From v0.1.0 to v0.8.0
item.description: MiBeeSteward is the device management and monitoring system I wrote for my own studio: one Go binary stringing network-device discovery, classification, monitoring, and management into a single line. v0.1.0 shipped on July 5, 2026; v0.8.0 landed on October 24 — eight minor releases and three patches evolving a “single-subnet scanner” into “a distributed system that passes enterprise audits”, then moving discovery into the router and probing out to the public egress. Each version used to have its own post; this one merges the v0.1.0–v0.8.0 release records into a single timeline: what each step did, and why.

item.title: MiBeeSteward v0.9.0: Phones Come and Go — the Asset Archive Remembers
item.description: The most numerous devices on a network aren’t servers — they’re phones, and the most transient ones too: on the office WiFi at nine in the morning, gone by six, absent all weekend. A phone upgrade leaves the old handset behind, never to connect again; a guest’s phone visited once, and never again. The old handling was blunt: offline past a threshold, the sweeper deleted the row, history included — and when the same phone ever connected again, it was a “new device”, with nothing to connect it to the last seen time, the old IP, the services it once ran.
